action.rationale: Cataloguing visible anomalies and comparing revision accounts performs the baseline's ordinary witness and material-feature comparison. The matrix adds bookkeeping.

observable.rationale: The procedure uses the same visible variants, material clues and correspondence. It does not invoke the available micro-probe or produce an additional observable.

inferential_warrant.rationale: Ordinary compatibility and conflict constrain revision sequences, while incomplete evidence limits reconstruction. A complete catalogue receives no additional evidential authority.

problem_decomposition.rationale: Organizing witnesses and revision accounts by anomaly makes the baseline comparison explicit without changing its units or dependencies.

next_inquiry.rationale: Further witness collation and consultation of correspondence are ordinary baseline actions. No new stopping condition or evidence-selection rule governs them.

materiality.rationale: The explicit matrix changes presentation and organization without changing evidence acquisition, admissible inference, uncertainty handling or subsequent inquiry.

native_reduction.closest_native_equivalent: Ordinary manuscript-genetic comparison of witnesses and material features against competing revision accounts, constrained by dated archival context.
native_reduction.rationale: Replacing the matrix with ordinary comparative notes preserves every specified epistemic operation and limitation. Probe availability does not distinguish the procedures, and the fixed procedure does not use it.

formalization.rationale: Indexing anomalies against accounts records ordinary disconfirmation reasoning. It imposes no additional intervention, evidential threshold, falsification criterion or next-step constraint.

anti_collapse.decisive_reason: The sole procedural addition is an explicit catalogue matrix; ordinary native comparison preserves its observations, compatibility judgments, limitations and follow-up actions without operational loss.
